notes: Scope: I encoded only reader-facing text (prose, check options/feedback/reveal, captions, aria-labels, noscript). The HTML comment 'MOUNT CONTRACT · w-sizing-sandbox' in s-04 contains builder-facing specifics (control list, step size 0.5 GB, default readouts like NODES 05 / RESERVED 38 OF 65 GB, and 'Expected values (ac-08)') that a reader never sees; I deliberately left these out. Consequently: (1) 'past 13 GB' is encoded as 13.5 GB (the reader text gives no step size; any value >13 is meant). (2) p1: the text says Fennel rents five nodes because of the requests, and the W-02 caption says a real cluster needs 'at least this many' as the sheet counts, so the sheet's count at default is implied to be ≤ 5; the text never states the default number. (3) 'All' ambiguity in p2 (set_to_use all) and p7 (halve every service): the prose says 'each request'/'every service', but the W-02 caption says the memory requests of payments and notifications stay as the teams set them and the aria-label says 'three services' memory requests'; so in W-02 'all' can at most cover storefront, orders and dispatch (the three are not named in reader text; inferred as the services other than payments and notifications). (4) p6 (k-04, doubling payments) points into W-02, but the W-02 caption says payments' memory request is not adjustable; I encoded the pointer as the text states it and flag the tension here without judging it. (5) p2's 'what sets that number?' implies the set_by readout is informative after the change (possibly no longer memory alone) but the text does not say what it becomes, so it is not encoded. p2's services_over count_eq 0 is implied by requests equalling use. (6) p3/p4 start: the three 'things to notice' are a list with no reset instruction between them, so I used 'previous'; they could also be read as independent from default. p3: the lead says the sheet counts the nodes needed 'plus one spare node', so switching it off implies nodes_total drops (by one) and nodes_for_pods is unchanged; 'by exactly one' is not expressible. (7) p8: 'another node on the bill' encoded as nodes_total (the bill counts what is rented, spare included); the text hedges with 'can mean' and 'on nodes that are already full'. p7: 'fewer nodes' is said of the cluster, applied to W-02 as implied. (8) Not encodable: bin-packing description ('W-02 does it to count the fewest nodes Fennel could manage with'); the caption's 'Each change places every Pod afresh'; 'Processor requests ... stay as the teams set them' (non-manipulable attributes); the idle bar is implied to sum to what the dashboard's 'less than a third busy' reflects (used < 1/3 of rented), but there is no observable for rented total. s-04's closing claim that requests closer to use 'would let Fennel rent fewer nodes, but not as few as possible' supports p2's implied decrease. No reader text mentions a Reset control.
